what: In a zero-gravity physics world, ten shapes (ball collider r .47 · mass .6 · move damping 4 · rotation damping 5 · friction 10) spawn at random positions and random directions 3~6 away from the center, and every frame each is pushed toward the center by its own position × −.05, clumping into one mass. Cursor position (z=0 coordinates spread to screen size) followed 5% per frame by a kinematic sphere (r .2) that pushes through the cluster so shapes step aside and then regroup. With fx:set, the old shapes fade out over 1s and the new shape group appears 1s later for 1s, flying in from outside and clustering

options.set: Shape set — a (plump dolls · bowls · tubs, default) · b (flat masks · rings)
options.radius: Collision ball radius, default .47 (group b is .9×)
options.scale: Image size ÷ collision ball, default 1.12 — the original scanned model is slightly larger than the ball, so they look overlapped
options.pull: Force pushing toward the center per frame (position × value), default .05
options.follow: Share the cursor sphere follows per frame, default .05
options.fade: Fade-out/fade-in length in seconds when switching groups — fade-in is delayed by the same amount, default 1
options.fov: Camera vertical field of view (deg), default 75
options.fx:set: Events sent to the element — turned into a bundle of detail.set. When physics is ready the element emits fx:ready (hook the loader here)

note: Shape colors mix --kf-accent-soft·--kf-dim·--kf-raised·--kf-ink-soft as glaze blotches. The original is a model with baked scan shadows, so it uses only even light (ambient 3), but default shapes have no baked shadow, so one upper-left light was added. rapier is 2MB, so it loads separately when attached (after three-global.js → three.cjs), and if it can’t load, the shapes only slide to the gathered spot over 2s and stand.
use: — load gsap · three-global.js · three.cjs first. When changing, el.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('fx:set', { detail: { set: 'b' } }))

from.where: index.html .cg-stage (series picker stage — pile of doll and mask scan models)
